answer: A refundable stake bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a deposit tied to one hardware-verified identity before answering. Like a ripple spreading outward, the cost of forging identities grows with every fake account, because each one needs its own locked deposit. A crystal-clear rule slashes the stake of any identity caught signing duplicates or spam, while honest agents get their deposit back. Even one umber-marked bad actor faces real financial loss, so mass identity forgery becomes economically irrational rather than free.
